_note: Committed so the flow can be reviewed without running graphify. The graphify graph merges this with an AST pass over the implementation.

hosts.host_shenostore: shenostore.shenodev.tech — storefront + owns the account lifecycle (TRD §4)
hosts.host_shenoflow: shenoflow.shenodev.tech — delivery agents and order tracking (PRD §1)

cookie.name: sheno_session
cookie.rationale: Domain=.shenodev.tech is what makes one login work on all three hosts; HttpOnly keeps the token out of client JS.

claims.tenant_id: tenant the session is scoped to — never from client input
claims.demo: true when this is the reserved Demo-mode session
claims.note: Owned by packages/auth and imported by all three apps (TRD §8). A redeclared copy in a second framework is the same divergence bug as a redeclared order-status enum.

flow: POST /api/auth/login with email + password to shenostore
look up users by (tenant_id, email) — schema §3
verify users.password_hash with Argon2id — nothing is minted before this passes
mint a JWT carrying the shared claim shape
Set-Cookie: sheno_session=<jwt>; Domain=.shenodev.tech; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
the browser presents the cookie to shenostore, shenoinventory and shenoflow
each app verifies the signature locally — no cross-app auth call (TRD §7)

nodes.label: shenostore.shenodev.tech — storefront + owns the account lifecycle (TRD §4)
shenoflow.shenodev.tech — delivery agents and order tracking (PRD §1)
SSO session cookie — HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Domain=.shenodev.tech
JWT — the token is the proof, the cookie is only the transport (TRD §7)
Session claim shape — a cross-app contract owned by packages/auth (TRD §8)
mintSession — signs a JWT for a verified user
verifySession — each app verifies the signature locally
No app calls another app to check 'am I logged in' (TRD §7)
POST /api/auth/login — the central auth route on ShenoStore
Demo mode mints a session carrying demo_tenant_id (TRD §7, RULE 5)
tenant_id comes from the session, never from client input (schema §3)
Token unreadable from client JS — HttpOnly (Plan Ph2 exit criteria)

edges.why: Auth / session / SSO is first-party and lives on ShenoStore (TRD §4).
Credentials are checked against users.password_hash before any token exists.
The route looks the user up by (tenant_id, email).
A successful password check mints the session.
The minted token carries the shared claim shape (TRD §8).
The token is transported in the cookie; the cookie is not the proof.
HttpOnly is what makes the token unreadable from client JS.
Domain=.shenodev.tech is what makes the browser send the cookie to every host.
Same cookie domain, so ShenoFlow receives it without a second login.
Each app verifies the signature and reads claims.
Each app verifies the signature and reads claims.
ShenoStore verifies too; it is not special-cased as the issuer.
A cross-app check turns every request into a cross-region round trip.
Verification reads the shared claim shape (TRD §8).
tenant_id is never taken from client input — it is read from the session.
Demo mode mints the same claim shape carrying demo_tenant_id.
Demo is a data tenant: the same tenant_id path, pointed at demo_tenant_id.
Never read the token into app state or expose it to client JS.

hyperedges.label: One credential, three hosts (PRD §3.1)
hyperedges.why: The cookie domain is the whole mechanism: scope it to .shenodev.tech and the browser presents it to all three apps, so no per-app login exists.

hyperedges.label: Login request path
hyperedges.why: Look up user -> verify Argon2id hash -> mint JWT -> set the shared cookie. Nothing is minted before the hash verifies.

hyperedges.label: Demo mode session (RULE 5)
hyperedges.why: Demo bypasses the password, never the tenant boundary: the session carries demo_tenant_id and every downstream query filters on it exactly as for any other tenant.
